title: Revision guards are workspace-wide: an unrelated task edit invalidates a captured revision for a task that never changed
description:
External report from the mbpm2 project, relayed by opum-agent 2026-09-15 18:50Z, listed among missing capabilities and described as the most concrete of them. REPRODUCED first-hand on quest 0.7.1 -- the report is accurate, and this task exists to record the measurement rather than the claim.

REPRODUCTION, in a disposable workspace with two unrelated tasks T-1 and T-2:
  capture T-1 revision via `quest task view T-1 --json` -> 6ab6e565...
  `quest task edit T-2 --add-note ...`                  -> exit 0   (T-2 only)
  `quest task edit T-1 --if-revision <T-1 revision>`    -> exit 5   CONFLICT
T-1 was never written to between the capture and the guarded edit. Editing an unrelated record invalidated it. The guard itself works correctly in the per-task sense too -- re-using an genuinely stale T-1 revision after T-1 moves also returns exit 5 -- so the mechanism is sound and only its SCOPE is wrong.

WHY IT MATTERS TO THE REPORTER: they run concurrent research sessions against one workspace. Workspace-wide scope means any two sessions writing different tasks conflict, so --if-revision is unusable as a safety mechanism precisely in the case it was built for. Its documented purpose (help text for task edit, QCLI-277) is stated in per-record terms -- "capture revision from an earlier task view --json, and the edit is refused ... if THE RECORD has moved since" -- so the implemented scope also contradicts the documentation.

ACCEPTANCE EXAMPLE, their shape: the sequence above returns exit 0 on the final command, because T-1 did not move. Exit 5 remains correct when T-1 itself has moved.

THE OTHER REPORTED GAPS -- field selection, note cursors, individual-note reads, zero-note projections -- are not reproduced here and are recorded on this task only as context. They should be separated into their own tasks if taken up; they are read-shaping conveniences, whereas this one is a correctness gap against the documented contract.

CONFIRMED WORKING in the same external report, evidence worth keeping because it is not otherwise available: an expanded 111-test suite with zero skips including real CLI integration tests, quest note limits, stale-write guards, typed proof relations, dependency traversal, version-drift warnings, and preservation of claim metadata. Their qualification tasks CON-52/53/54 are Done. Full report at results/analysis/proof-graph-pilot-20260913/build-validation/lore-0.7.0-quest-0.7.1-20260915/validation-report.md on their side.

acceptanceCriteria.text: --if-revision is scoped to the record being written: editing an unrelated task does not invalidate a captured revision, demonstrated by the two-task reproduction returning exit 0 on the final command
Exit 5 is still returned when the guarded record itself has moved since the revision was captured, proven as a separate run rather than inferred from the first
The help text for task edit and the workspace docs agree with the implemented scope, since they currently describe per-record behavior that the implementation does not provide
The reporter is told the result either way, including if the workspace-wide scope turns out to be load-bearing for something and cannot narrow
